statement.p: Find a number a so that the change of variables s=x+ay, t=y transforms the integral \int\int_R \,dx\,dy over the parallelogram R in the xy-plane with vertices (0,0), (10,0), (-18,8), (-8,8) into an integral \int\int_T \left\vert \frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right\vert\,ds\,dt over a rectangle T in the st-plane.

static.solution:
x = s-at, y=t. The four edges of R are y=0, y=8, y=-\frac{4}{9} x, y=-\frac{4}{9} (x-10). The change of variables transforms the edges to t=0, t=8, t=-\frac{4}{9} s + \frac{4}{9} at, t=-\frac{4}{9} s + \frac{4}{9} at + \frac{40}{9}. These are equations for the edges of a rectangle in the st-plane if the last two are of the form: s=(\hbox{Constant}). This happens when the t terms drop out, or a=\frac{9}{4}. With a=\frac{9}{4} the change of variables gives \int\int_T \left\vert \frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right\vert \,ds\,dt over the rectangle T: 0\le t \le 8, 0\le s\le 10.
The jacobian \left\vert\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right\vert is \left\vert\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right\vert = \left\vert\begin{array}{cc} 1 \amp -\frac{9}{4} \\ 0 \amp 1 \end{array} \right\vert = 1.
